component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007): duplexes and single-family attached houses (made consistent with duplexes) in residential districts, residential infill and district-intensity changes, flag lots with narrower poles, the Small House/Small Lot option restructured as a small-lot bonus
coverage: City of Durham: residential districts in the urban tier, and RU-5 and RU-5(2) in the suburban tier
coding_notes: City Council approved 6-1 on 2019-09-03. Case TC1800007 (one city notice says TC1800005, apparently a typo). component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007): ADUs up to 800 sq ft (countywide provision)
coverage: City of Durham, all districts where ADUs are allowed (the 800 sq ft allowance applies county-wide); not with a duplex or the 2,000 sq ft small-lot bonus option
coding_notes: City Council approved 6-1 on 2019-09-03. Effective date not stated on the city page and the ordinance (Attachment B) could not be opened (Durham DocumentCenter returns 403; durham.municipal.codes is offline): effective_date is coded as the vote date. Case TC1800007 (one city notice says TC1800005, apparently a typo). Planning Commission 12-1 on 2019-06-11. ADUs per lot, detached allowance, owner occupancy and parking were not on the city page and stay empty.

component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007) adopted by the Durham County Board of Commissioners for the unincorporated county (joint Durham UDO)
coverage: Unincorporated Durham County: residential districts in the urban tier and RU-5/RU-5(2) in the suburban tier
coding_notes: Board of County Commissioners approved 5-0 at a rescheduled hearing on 2019-10-28 (city EHC page). Effective date not found: coded as the vote date. Same provisions as NC-3719000-missing_middle-2019.

component: Expanding Housing Choices (TC1800007): ADUs up to 800 sq ft, unincorporated Durham County
coverage: Unincorporated Durham County, districts where ADUs are allowed
coding_notes: County vote 5-0 on 2019-10-28; effective date not found, coded as the vote date. Same provisions as NC-3719000-adu-2019.

component: Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD, TC2200001): minimum off-street parking requirements eliminated citywide for new development
parking: No minimum parking requirements
coverage: City of Durham, citywide
coding_notes: Council vote 'minutes to midnight on Monday, November 20, 2023' (Strong Towns, 2023-11-21). The round-3 brief lists 2023-11-21 (the day it was reported); coded 2023-11-20. A 4-3 tally appears only in a search snippet (Axios, not opened). Effective date not found: coded as the vote date. Privately initiated text amendment TC2200001 (city notice 2022-11-23).

component: SCAD (TC2200001): larger ADUs (proposed cap 1,200 sq ft and two stories, up from 800 sq ft and one story) and ADUs allowed with places of worship
coverage: City of Durham
coding_notes: The 1,200 sq ft / two-story figures are from coverage of the proposal (IndyWeek, March 2023); the County board's December 2023 adoption is reported as allowing 'bigger ADUs'. The adopted text was not read, so adu_max_sqft stays empty until it is. Effective date not found: coded as the vote date.

component: TC-16-19, Ord. (2020) 117 TC 432: ADUs by right in residential districts, attached, detached or over a garage, one per lot, up to 1,000 sq ft depending on lot size; owner-occupancy requirement struck
coverage: City of Raleigh, residential districts R-1 to R-10
coding_notes: Adopted 2020-07-07 (UDO Supplement 11; sections 1.3.3, 1.5.2, 2.1.3, 2.6.3, 5.1.1, Art. 5.7), vote 6-1 (IndyWeek). Effective date not found: the city says text changes 'typically' take effect 5 days after adoption (about 2020-07-12); coded as the adoption date. adu_max_sqft=1000 is the largest cap (current Sec. 2.6.3: 1,000 sq ft on lots over 40,000 sq ft, 800 otherwise, and smaller than the main house); the 2020 lot-size tiers were not read. lot_split=False and no parking minimum come from the current Sec. 2.6.3 (later amendments, tag TC-1-25), not the 2020 text: parking left empty. Not allowed on flag lots (current text).

component: TC-5-20, Ord. (2021) 263 TC 451 (Missing Middle): attached houses (duplexes) in R-2 and R-4, townhouses in R-6 (and in R-2 in compact, conservation or cottage-court developments), apartments in R-10 on smaller lots; units-per-acre limits removed in every residential district except R-1; one ADU per lot regardless of density
coverage: City of Raleigh residential districts R-2, R-4, R-6 and R-10 (R-1 keeps its density limit)
coding_notes: Ordinance states 'Adopted: July 6, 2021' and 'Effective: August 5, 2021' (Sec. 43: 30 days after adoption). Lot size and area per unit now control yield (minimum lot area R-1 40,000, R-2 20,000, R-4 10,000, R-6 6,000 sq ft; lot-area-per-unit rows of 2,500/2,000/1,500 sq ft not mapped to districts), so unit_cap and min_lot_sqft stay empty. Parking: only parking setbacks changed. by_right and lot_split not coded (the ordinance lists permitted building types; review path not read).

component: TC-20-21, Ord. (2022) 362 TC 466 (Missing Middle 2.0): tiny houses (≤800 sq ft footprint, ≤1,200 sq ft floor area) as one or two units with smaller minimum lots, flag lots for tiny houses, two-unit townhouses in R-4, ADUs on townhouse lots, a Frequent Transit Development Option (20% of units beyond 12 affordable at 60% AMI for 30 years)
coverage: City of Raleigh residential districts; the development option in Frequent Transit Areas
coding_notes: Ordinance states 'Adopted: May 10, 2022' and 'Effective: August 8, 2022' (Sec. 41: 90 days after adoption); the city FAQ agrees. Tiny-house minimum lot area: R-1 40,000, R-2 15,000, R-4 7,500, R-6 3,000 (from 4,500), R-10 2,000 (from 3,000) sq ft as read from the redline (strike-through extraction ambiguous for R-6 and R-10), so min_lot_sqft stays empty. lot_split=True reads the new flag lots for tiny houses as allowing new small lots. Approval is administrative per the FAQ; by_right not coded.

component: TC-20-21: two ADUs per lot in a Frequent Transit Area (only one attached); ADUs allowed on townhouse lots; no ADUs on flag lots
coverage: City of Raleigh, lots in Frequent Transit Areas (two ADUs); townhouse lots in residential districts
coding_notes: Dates as NC-3755000-missing_middle-2022. adus_per_lot=2 applies only in Frequent Transit Areas; elsewhere one per lot (NC-3755000-adu-2020). Size rules unchanged from 2020 as far as read.

component: Unified Development Ordinance: duplexes and triplexes allowed on lots in the Neighborhood 1 (N1) districts that replaced the single-family districts (R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-8 → N1-A to N1-D; UR-1 → N1-E)
coverage: City of Charlotte, Neighborhood 1 districts (conventional districts only; conditional districts keep their legacy rules)
coding_notes: Adopted 6-4 on 2022-08-22, effective 2023-06-01 (Charlotte Regional Business Alliance); the city's UDO page is behind bot protection and was not opened. The translation of legacy districts is UDO Table 3-1 (text amendment 2023-174, p. 49). Triplex conditions in the 2022 text (e.g. lot or corner requirements) and N1 parking minimums were not read: by_right, min_lot_sqft and parking stay empty. In March 2024 staff proposed limiting triplexes to corner lots in N1-A to N1-D (Charlotte Ledger, WFAE); text amendment 2024-067 (reported decided 2024-06-24) was not opened, so no superseding row yet. V5 holdout reform: Charlotte outcomes from 2023-06-01 are hidden.

component: UDO (Art. 15.6): one ADU per lot with a single-family house in any district, or with a duplex not on a sublot; same ownership as the principal house; internal ADU ≤40% and detached ≤50% of the principal house's floor area
coverage: City of Charlotte, all districts with a single-family house (or a duplex not on a sublot)
coding_notes: Rules from the city's (undated) UDO accessory-structure permit form, whose file name ('udoamended') suggests it may reflect later amendments. Same-ownership rule is not an owner-occupancy requirement: owner_occ left empty. No absolute size cap: adu_max_sqft empty. No separate driveway except corner or alley lots; no taller than the principal house. Parking not mentioned. Charlotte allowed ADUs before the UDO; the pre-UDO rules were not coded.

component: Land Development Ordinance ADU amendment: owner occupancy no longer required, size up to 50% of the principal house (400 sq ft minimum removed), no additional parking, accessory-building setbacks and height
parking: No additional parking space required
coverage: City of Greensboro, all residential districts
coding_notes: Council approved unanimously on 2024-04-16 (WFDD). Effective date and ordinance number not found: coded as the vote date. ADUs stay allowed attached or detached in all residential districts through a residential building permit only (by right). Size cap is relative (50% of the principal house), so adu_max_sqft is empty. ADUs per lot not stated.

component: S.L. 2026-59 (S445, Regulatory Reform Act of 2026) Sec. 44, new G.S. 160D-917: at least one ADU per single-family detached house in residential zones; no conditional zoning, no parking minimums, no ban on renting house and ADU separately long-term, fees no higher than for a single-family house; local size cap must be 800-1,000 sq ft; no separate subdivision
parking: No minimum parking or parking restrictions
coverage: Charlotte: single-family detached houses in areas zoned residential; not in historic preservation districts or National Historic Landmarks; private covenants unaffected
coding_notes: S.L. 2026-59 (S445) Sec. 44, new G.S. 160D-917, applied to Charlotte only: the law covers non-coastal cities of 50,000 or more (2020 Census and 2025 estimate both at or above 50,000).
